paragraphs: Friend, look at what this chapter hands us. One sleepless night, one book picked off the shelf, and one line about Mordecai that nobody had paid attention to. The Bible never says God arranged any of it, so I won't say that. But I will say this: Mordecai's good deed was written down (Esther 6:2), and it was still there when the king needed it.

Now look at Haman. He hears the king ask, "What should be done for the man whom the king is delighted to honor?" and he thinks, "Whom would the king be delighted to honor more than me?" (Esther 6:6). Friend, that's a man so full of himself he has no room left to see what's coming, and I know, because I've had a few days like that with a batch of snickerdoodles. Haman built everything on his own plans, and by the end of the chapter his head is covered in grief (Esther 6:12).

So here's what I'm taking out of the oven today. Doing right can feel like it vanishes. Pride feels like it's winning. But this passage shows us that neither one is the end of the story. Keep doing right when nobody claps, baker, because Scripture says even Haman's own wife and advisers told him, "you will surely fall before him" (Esther 6:13), and the story isn't over yet.
